content:
mike_ops: @here urgent: sharp spike in 5xx on /v2/prompt-route since the v4 canary started at ~2951234560. Canary toggle 'prompt_v4_route' at 10% — streaming clients returning many 502/504. Paging oncall.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: prompt_v4_route -> 10% (user-slices). Healthcheck summary: 502 x 42 in last 1m, latency spike to p95 1.2s. Recommend rollback or kill-flag.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: P-3872 ALERT - High error rate on production route. Paging jonathan_oncall, emily_se.

jonathan_oncall: Oncall here - looking. Can someone grab the canary group logs (nginx + runtime) and the metric window for the last 5m? Any customer-facing errors reported yet?

emily_se: Support flagged ~15 tickets referencing "model timeout" and "stream closed". New endpoint uses different chunking / client keepalive; I'm seeing connection resets in the nginx upstreams.

mike_ops: We should kill the feature flag now if customers are impacted. @jonathan_oncall want me to flip prompt_v4_route to off?

jonathan_oncall: I'll flip it. Doing emergency kill now — one sec.

jonathan_oncall: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://flags.internal/api/v1/toggles/prompt_v4_route/override" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -d '{"action":"force_off","reason":"emergency-5xx-canary","actor":"jonathan_oncall"}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Received feature-flag override request for prompt_v4_route by jonathan_oncall. Applying override... OK.

sre-bot: sre-bot: FeatureFlag(prompt_v4_route) set to FORCED_OFF (scope=global) by jonathan_oncall at 2026-03-15T01:12:30Z. Traffic should failover to stable route.

emily_se: Confirming traffic rerouted to stable model. Watching metrics / logs now.

mike_ops: Metrics: 5xx dropped back to baseline within ~30s after the flag flip. Good catch. Support, which customers saw errors?

andrew_support: Affected customers: cust-alpha, cust-delta, cust-gamma, cust-omega, cust-zeta — total 9 distinct customers surfaced in automatic alerts. I have replied to all with a short note: we've routed you back to the stable endpoint and are investigating root cause.

carla_pm: I'll post a concise status update to status.redwood.ai: "We observed errors during canary of PromptV4 routing; traffic reverted to stable and engineering is investigating." Drafting now.

jonathan_oncall: Taking incident owner. Emily - can you reproduce locally against the canary handler? Please grab canary-instance ids, nginx upstream reset traces, and any kernel/socket level logs.

emily_se: On it. Early hypothesis: the promptv4 handler uses a new HTTP/2 streaming layer that mismatches keepalive expectations -> client-side EOFs. Reproducing with a staged client now.

mike_ops: Create dedicated incident channel and set severity. Add postmortem owner.

andrew_support: Sent targeted customer updates. I'll compile the ticket list and sample error traces to include in the postmortem.

jonathan_oncall: :thumbsup: Pager resolved for now. Keeping thread open for triage and RCA. If metrics spike again, re-ping.

sre-bot: sre-bot: Incident P-3872 updated to state=triage, severity=P2. Pager cleared.

carla_pm: Postmortem owner = jonathan_oncall. Target ETA for draft = 72h. Action items (initial): 1) revert endpoint changes in next deploy until streaming test coverage added; 2) add integration tests for HTTP/2 streaming with idle/keepalive cases; 3) improve canary telemetry for streaming endpoints; 4) update rollout playbook to include kill-switch procedure checklist. I'll create tickets and assign.

jonathan_oncall: I'll take the RCA and link logs + timeline. Thanks everyone — nice quick kill-and-recover.
